## `host`

`string`, default `localhost`

The relay hostname or address. Required when mail is enabled.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    host: "localhost"
```

## `port`

`int`, default `25`

The relay port: conventionally 25 for a local relay, 587 for submission with STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    port: 25
```

## `tls`

`string`, default `opportunistic`

The transport policy — one of off, opportunistic (default), required, or implicit.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    tls: "opportunistic"
```

## `server_name`

`string`, default `empty`

Overrides the name the relay's certificate is verified against. Needed only when Host is an address rather than the name on the certificate.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    server_name: "smtp.example.com"
```

## `ca_file`

`string`, default `empty`

A PEM bundle to verify the relay's certificate against, for a relay using a private CA. Empty uses the system trust store.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    ca_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem"
```

## `insecure_skip_verify`

`bool`, default `false`

Disables verification of the relay's certificate. It turns TLS into obfuscation — an attacker who can redirect the connection can also present their own certificate — so it exists for a lab with a self-signed relay and is warned about at startup.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    insecure_skip_verify: false
```

## `auth`

`string`, default `none`

Selects the SASL mechanism — one of none (default), auto, plain, login, cram-md5, scram-sha-1, scram-sha-256, or xoauth2. "auto" negotiates the strongest mechanism the relay advertises.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    auth: "none"
```

## `username`

`string`, default `empty`

The SASL username. Required for every mechanism but none.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    username: "ssoossh@example.com"
```

## `password`

`string`, default `empty`

The SASL password, or the OAuth2 token for xoauth2. Prefer `smtp.password_file`: this value is a secret sitting in a config file.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    password: ""
```

## `password_file`

`string`, default `empty`

Reads the password from a file instead, so the secret can be a mounted file or a systemd credential rather than config text. Takes precedence over Password when both are set. Read once at startup; trailing whitespace is trimmed, since an editor's newline is never part of the password.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    password_file: "/run/secrets/ssoossh-smtp-password"
```

## `helo`

`string`, default `empty`

The name announced in the EHLO/HELO greeting. Empty lets go-mail use the local hostname, which is right unless the relay checks it against something specific.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    helo: "ssoossh.example.com"
```

## `timeout`

`duration`, default `15s`

Bounds a single delivery's connect-and-send. It bounds only the background sender, never a request: nothing a browser or an unattended job waits on is behind this.

```yaml
mail:
  smtp:
    timeout: 15s
```
